description: Airhand: high-performance, low-latency remote desktop over QUIC (controller and host in one program)
notes: The Windows host must run as the "Airhand" system service, so this package needs administrator rights to install, update and uninstall. Installing registers the service, a system-wide "Start with Windows" entry and a firewall rule; uninstalling removes all three.

Keep the tray closed before "scoop update airhand": Scoop skips the update while an Airhand process from the package directory is running. Starting Airhand from the start menu opens the console; the tray entry is "Open console".

Scoop unpacks the official NSIS installer instead of running it, and calls "airhand.exe --install" itself. The install directory stays under Scoop, so version rollbacks keep working and the service path follows the current version.
config.toml holds this computer's control code, its end-to-end identity and paired controllers. It is persisted, so it survives updates and uninstall unless "scoop uninstall --purge" is used.
pre_install: # "#/dl.7z" only renames the download; Scoop will not auto-extract a .exe, so unpack the NSIS
# payload here (same approach as the other Electron/Tauri manifests in this bucket).
# The service reads config.toml from its own directory, so restore the persisted copy before
# "--install" runs. persist_data would otherwise replace this file with a directory junction.

script: # Wrap in a scriptblock: "break" inside a plain if would unwind the whole install.
if (!(is_admin)) { throw "Airhand needs administrator rights to $app $cmd." }
# Register and start the "Airhand" system service, mirroring the official installer.

post_install: # Drop the installer scaffolding, not the program.

script: if (!(is_admin)) { throw "Airhand needs administrator rights to $app $cmd." }
# Stops and deletes the service and removes the system-wide startup entry.
